# Results — Study 907 (Senior Loans vs High-Yield) on the real total-return tapes

*Generated by [`examples/verify.py`](../examples/verify.py). One question — do **senior secured
loans** (BKLN, SRLN), which sit *above* high-yield bonds in the capital stack at a similar
yield, actually pay you a **seniority premium** — a real risk-adjusted edge over high-yield
(HYG, JNK)? — run on the **total-return** tapes, every Sharpe measured **excess of cash**
(BIL, the 1-3m T-bill ETF). Everything is raced on the **common window bounded by BKLN's
2011-03-03 inception**, so the HY arms don't get to bank the 2008 GFC the loan arms never
saw. Data as-of 2026-06-30 (last complete month; the partial July 2026 bar is dropped). Match
the fingerprint to confirm you hold the same tapes.*

## Data stamp

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Real tape | yfinance daily **total-return** closes (`auto_adjust=True`): BKLN, SRLN, HYG, JNK, IEF, BIL — public, no key |
| Loan sleeve | **BKLN** (Invesco Senior Loan, lists 2011-03-03) + **SRLN** (SPDR Blackstone Senior Loan, lists **2013-04-04** — joins the composite mid-sample) |
| HY sleeve | **HYG** (iShares iBoxx HY) + **JNK** (SPDR Bloomberg HY) |
| Cash leg | **BIL** (SPDR 1-3m T-bill) — every Sharpe is **excess of BIL** |
| Window | **2011-03-03 → 2026-06-30**, 3,854 daily rows · Fingerprint `e09ddb919d86` |
| Inference | Newey-West **HAC *t*** (10 lags) on the return spread; circular block bootstrap (21-day blocks, 5,000 draws) on the excess-Sharpe advantage |
| Costs | long-loans/short-HY: monthly round-trip 2 × one-way × NAV + borrow on the short HY leg |

> **Short-history / survivorship caveat (Signal axis).** SRLN only lists 2013, so the loan
> composite is BKLN-only for its first two years; all four credit ETFs are *live survivors*
> (no defaulted/closed loan fund in the sample). The effect is a per-day property of two live
> sleeves, so survivorship bias is mild — but the sample is one 15-year regime of falling
> then rising rates, honestly named.

## The arms — total return, excess-of-cash Sharpe, 2011–2026

| Arm | CAGR | Vol | Sharpe (excess) | Max drawdown |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| BKLN (loan) | 3.71% | **5.8%** | +0.414 | −24.2% |
| SRLN (loan) | 3.79% | **5.4%** | +0.411 | −22.3% |
| **LOANS composite** | **3.82%** | **5.4%** | **+0.457** | −23.2% |
| HYG (HY) | 4.72% | 8.2% | +0.431 | −22.0% |
| JNK (HY) | 4.61% | 8.1% | +0.421 | −22.9% |
| **HY composite** | **4.67%** | **8.1%** | **+0.428** | −22.5% |
| IEF (duration ref) | 2.38% | 6.5% | +0.177 | −23.9% |

The loan sleeve's **lower volatility is real and large** — 5.4% vs 8.1%, a third less risk
than HY. But its **CAGR is a full point lower** (3.82% vs 4.67%): the seniority discount buys
calm, not extra carry. The two forces very nearly cancel in the Sharpe.

## The seniority race — is the risk-adjusted edge real?

| Construction | Sharpe loans | Sharpe HY | **advantage** | return spread (loans−HY) | NW *t* |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| **Flagship** BKLN vs HYG | +0.414 | +0.431 | **−0.017** | −1.14 %/yr | −0.95 |
| **Composite** (BKLN,SRLN) vs (HYG,JNK) | +0.457 | +0.428 | **+0.029** | −1.00 %/yr | −0.83 |

The Sharpe advantage is a **rounding error whose sign flips with construction** — HY noses
ahead on the flagship single pair, loans nose ahead on the two-ETF composite. And the
**return spread is negative** either way (loans earn ~1 %/yr *less*, NW *t* ≈ −0.9), so
there is no *carry* premium to seniority — if anything a small negative one.

**Bootstrap on the composite advantage** (21-day circular blocks, 5,000 draws):
advantage **+0.029**, 95% CI **[−0.258, +0.470]**, loans win in **62 %** of resamples. The
interval **straddles zero comfortably** — the risk-adjusted advantage is statistically
indistinguishable from a coin flip.

## Era robustness — the sign is consistent but never significant

| Era | n | Sharpe loans | Sharpe HY | advantage | spread NW *t* |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| 2011–15 (energy build-up) | 1,216 | +0.54 | +0.43 | +0.10 | −0.49 |
| 2016–19 | 1,006 | +1.64 | +1.16 | +0.48 | −1.38 |
| 2020–22 (COVID + hike) | 756 | +0.05 | −0.09 | +0.13 | +0.49 |
| 2023–26 | 875 | +0.96 | +0.69 | +0.27 | +0.27 → −0.44 |

The loan sleeve's Sharpe **edges HY's in every era** (a genuinely era-consistent *sign*),
but the margins are small, and in **no era** does the return spread clear even |*t*| = 2.
Era-consistent noise is still noise: the advantage is a lower-vol artifact, not a premium
that the tape confirms.

## Where seniority helps — and where it bites (total return through the stress episodes)

| Episode | BKLN | SRLN | HYG | JNK |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| Energy default wave 2015-06 → 2016-02 | **−6.8%** | **−5.3%** | −12.1% | −15.0% |
| COVID liquidity crash 2020-02-19 → 03-23 | **−23.8%** | −22.3% | −21.9% | −22.8% |
| 2022 rate shock 2022-01 → 2022-10 | **−4.5%** | −7.4% | −14.6% | −15.8% |

This is the honest split. When the pain is **spread- or rate-driven**, seniority and the
floating coupon deliver exactly as advertised: loans lost roughly **half** what HY lost in
the 2015-16 energy wave and in the 2022 rate shock. But in the one **pure liquidity crisis**
(COVID), the loan sleeve — the *less liquid* leg, sold at forced-seller discounts — gapped
**as hard or harder** than HY (BKLN −23.8% vs HYG −21.9%), precisely when seniority was
supposed to protect you. Recovery/seniority is a *solvency-cycle* feature that a liquidity
run inverts.

## Tradability — the natural trade loses money

Long loans / short HY (dollar-neutral), the only way to actually *harvest* "seniority":

| Cost schedule | gross | net | NW *t* | net Sharpe |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| 5 bps/side + 60 bps borrow | −1.02 %/yr | **−2.82 %/yr** | −2.34 | −0.49 |
| 3 bps/side + 40 bps borrow | −1.02 %/yr | **−2.14 %/yr** | −1.77 | −0.37 |

The gross spread is **already negative** (loans earn less), so no cost schedule rescues it —
after borrow on the short HY leg the trade loses **2–3 %/yr**. The loan sleeve's only genuine
advantage is *risk-adjusted* (lower vol), which a dollar-neutral book cannot monetize.

## Synthetic control (machinery only — never supports the stamp)

A deterministic loans/HY/cash world (shared credit factor, loan leg engineered to *lower vol*
with a tunable `sharpe_edge`). **Null** (`edge=0`, lower vol exactly offset by lower carry —
same Sharpe), 12 seeds: mean Sharpe advantage **−0.061** (sd 0.253) — no systematic edge, the
detector is unbiased. **Planted** (`edge=0.6`, seed 907): advantage **+0.334**, loans win the
bootstrap in **93 %** of resamples. The estimator finds a real edge when one is planted and
finds nothing when none is — which is why we trust its verdict of *nothing* on the real tape.

## Verdict

- **Signal — is the seniority premium a real risk-adjusted edge? → WEAK.** The loan sleeve's
  lower volatility is real (5.4% vs 8.1%) and it cushions rate/spread selloffs — but the
  excess-Sharpe advantage is a rounding error (**+0.029**) whose **sign flips with
  construction**, its bootstrap CI **[−0.26, +0.47] straddles zero**, and the *return* spread
  is **negative** (−1 %/yr, NW *t* −0.83). Loans and HY are, risk-adjusted, a **wash**; the
  "premium" is a vol reshuffle, not a higher risk-adjusted return.
- **Tradability — is it bankable? → MIRAGE.** The harvestable long-loans/short-HY spread is
  negative gross and **−2 to −3 %/yr** after borrow + costs. The only real edge (lower vol)
  cannot be captured dollar-neutral; costs and the negative carry erase it.
- **"Seniority = a free risk-adjusted premium?" → BUSTED.** Seniority + the floating coupon
  genuinely halve your loss in rate/spread selloffs (2015-16 energy, 2022) — a real defensive
  tilt — but you pay for it in lower total return *and* the loan sleeve gaps **worse** in the
  one pure liquidity crisis (2020), exactly when you wanted the protection.

> **In one sentence:** senior loans really are the calmer, lower-vol, rate-proof cousin of
> high-yield and they shine when the pain is spreads or rates — but they earn **less** total
> return, **tie** on risk-adjusted return (a bootstrap that can't tell them apart from HY),
> and gap **harder** in a liquidity run, so the "seniority premium" is a genuine *volatility*
> discount, not a harvestable *edge*.
